contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

Assign each bike courier a single restaurant and a single delivery zone so that every restaurant is handled by a single courier and every zone is covered by a single courier, and keep the total riding distance as small as possible.

As conference organizer, assign each keynote speaker a single room and a single time slot so that every room is allocated to a single speaker and every time slot hosts a single speaker, and minimize the overall scheduling cost.
For each product pick a single machine and a single shift so that every machine is dedicated to a single product and every shift is used for a single product, and minimize the total production cost.

Match each student with a single project and a single supervisor so that every project is taken by a single student and every supervisor mentors a single student, while keeping the total mismatch penalty as low as possible.

For each model choose a single photographer and a single backdrop so that every photographer shoots a single model and every backdrop is used by a single model, and minimize the overall expected retouch time.

Assign each dining table a single appetizer vendor and a single dessert vendor so that every appetizer vendor serves a single table and every dessert vendor serves a single table, and minimize the total catering expense.
For each pallet select a single truck and a single route so that every truck carries a single pallet and every route is used by a single pallet, with the goal of minimizing total fuel cost.

For each client choose a single outfit and a single accessory so that every outfit is worn by a single client and every accessory is assigned to a single client, and minimize the combined wardrobe cost.
Assign each band a single stage and a single time slot so that each stage hosts a single band and each time slot features a single band, and minimize the sum of expected scheduling conflict costs.

For each document pick a single translator and a single language pair so that every translator handles a single document and every language pair is used for a single document, minimizing the total translation expense.

For each customer order assign a single printer and a single finishing station so that every printer processes a single order and every finishing station handles a single order, and minimize total processing time.
For each ad campaign choose a single channel and a single week so that every channel runs a single campaign and every week carries a single campaign, and minimize the overall advertising spend.

Assign each family member a single household task and a single cleaning day so that every task is assigned to a single family member and every cleaning day is claimed by a single family member, while minimizing total inconvenience.

For each restaurant table assign a single waiter and a single wine pairing so that every waiter serves a single table and every wine pairing is matched to a single table, and minimize total service time.

Assign each course a single classroom and a single time slot so that every classroom hosts a single course and every time slot is used by a single course, minimizing the sum of students' schedule conflict costs.

For each scene choose a single director of photography and a single shooting location so that every director of photography shoots a single scene and every location is used for a single scene, and minimize total setup cost.
For each daily menu assign a single chef and a single supplier so that every chef prepares a single menu and every supplier supplies a single menu, minimizing total ingredient cost.

For each patient pick a single specialist and a single appointment room so that every specialist sees a single patient and every room is occupied by a single patient, and minimize total expected wait and transfer cost.

Assign each content creator a single camera kit and a single editing slot so that every kit is used by a single creator and every editing slot is taken by a single creator, minimizing overall turnaround time.
For each prototype choose a single tester and a single test rig so that every tester evaluates a single prototype and every rig is used for a single prototype, and minimize the sum of testing costs.
Match each photo shoot to a single photographer and a single equipment kit, with every photographer and every kit used by a single shoot, aiming to minimize the sum of rental and labor costs.
For each delivery order choose a single driver and a single van, guaranteeing that every driver and every van is assigned to a single order, and pick assignments to minimize total fuel and time cost.

As the event organizer, pair each activity with a single volunteer and a single station so that every volunteer and every station serves a single activity, and set assignments to keep aggregate staffing cost as small as possible.
Assign each package a single courier and a single route, ensuring each courier and each route handles a single package, and choose the assignments to minimize cumulative transit cost.
For each repair request allocate a single technician and a single tool kit, with every technician and every kit allocated to a single request, and allocate to minimize overall service cost.

Organize for each meeting a single presenter and a single meeting room, ensuring every presenter and every room is booked for a single meeting, and schedule to minimize total preparation and travel cost.
Match each film scene to a single actor and a single costume, so that every actor and every costume appears in a single scene, and choose pairings to minimize the combined casting and wardrobe cost.
Assign to each customer a single interpreter and a single time slot, with every interpreter and every time slot used by a single customer, and arrange these to minimize the total interpretation cost.
As the campus scheduler, assign each exam a single proctor and a single hall, with every proctor and every hall used for a single exam, and plan to minimize overall supervision and room costs.
Allocate for each patient a single nurse and a single room, ensuring every nurse and every room cares for a single patient, and make assignments to minimize the total staffing and accommodation cost.

Match each song in the concert to a single musician and a single instrument, so that every musician and every instrument performs a single song, and arrange the lineup to minimize the sum of rehearsal and rental costs.
For each art commission designate a single artist and a single frame, with every artist and every frame committed to a single commission, and select pairings to minimize the total commissioning cost.
Assign each shipment a single container and a single loading dock, ensuring every container and every dock is used for a single shipment, and arrange to minimize overall handling and transport cost.
Match each tutoring session to a single tutor and a single textbook, with every tutor and every textbook assigned to a single session, and plan these matches to minimize the total tutoring cost.

For each house to be painted choose a single crew and a single paint color, so that every crew and every color is used for a single house, and pick assignments to minimize total labor and material cost.

As the neighborhood grocery coordinator, assign for each online order a single courier and a single dropoff window so that overall delivery expense is as small as possible, ensuring each courier is assigned to a single order and each dropoff window is assigned to a single order.

Help the community theater producer allocate for each rehearsal a single rehearsal room and a single technician in order to minimize total setup and staffing cost, with every room used by a single rehearsal and every technician assigned to a single rehearsal.

As the wedding planner, choose for each reception table a single caterer and a single dessert option to keep total catering expense at a minimum, and make sure each caterer handles a single table and each dessert option is used for a single table.

In the school office, match for each class a single classroom and a single teaching assistant so that the combined running cost is minimized, with each classroom hosting a single class and each assistant supporting a single class.

As the community health coordinator, assign for each home visit a single nurse and a single equipment kit to minimize total operational cost, making sure each nurse is scheduled for a single visit and each equipment kit is used in a single visit.

Ask the museum curator to decide for each exhibit space a single artwork and a single lighting setup so that total installation cost is minimized, while each artwork goes to a single space and each lighting setup is installed in a single space.

In the small factory, assign for each production order a single machine and a single operator to keep total processing cost as low as possible, with each machine processing a single order and each operator working on a single order.

Ask the volunteer coordinator to pair for each outreach location a single volunteer and a single vehicle so that the total travel and coordination cost is minimized, ensuring every volunteer is assigned to a single location and every vehicle is used for a single location.

As the boutique manager, select for each customer a single stylist and a single fitting room to minimize combined staffing and space cost, with each stylist allocated to a single customer and each fitting room reserved for a single customer.

Ask the film festival director to schedule for each screening a single technician and a single projector model to minimize total equipment and crew cost, ensuring each technician is assigned to a single screening and each projector model is used in a single screening.

As the tech startup lead, allocate for each task a single developer and a single testing environment so that overall development and testing cost is minimized, and make sure each developer works on a single task and each testing environment is used for a single task.

Request the campus housing officer to assign for each incoming student a single dorm room and a single roommate pairing option to minimize total housing allocation cost, with each dorm room assigned to a single student and each roommate pairing option applied to a single student.

As the garden center owner, match for each landscaping job a single plant supplier and a single delivery date to minimize cumulative procurement and delivery cost, ensuring each supplier serves a single job and each delivery date is used for a single job.

Ask the fashion show coordinator to allocate for each model a single outfit and a single backstage assistant so that total preparation and staffing cost is as low as possible, while each outfit is worn by a single model and each assistant supports a single model.

As the community library manager, choose for each reading session a single storyteller and a single seating arrangement to minimize overall event cost, making sure every storyteller leads a single session and every seating arrangement is used for a single session.

Request the city market coordinator to assign for each vendor a single stall and a single electricity hookup schedule to minimize total marketplace operating cost, ensuring each stall is occupied by a single vendor and each hookup schedule is assigned to a single vendor.

As the photography studio owner, schedule for each client a single photographer and a single backdrop so that total booking and setup cost is minimized, with each photographer assigned to a single client and each backdrop reserved for a single client.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.description: problem size (same size for i/j/k sets)

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of couriers (equal to the number of restaurants and the number of delivery zones). This is the problem size: how many one-to-one courier→restaurant→zone assignments are needed.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers used for the indices in the instance (labels or codes that identify each courier/restaurant/zone). These IDs index the i (couriers), j (restaurants) and k (delivery zones) sets.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the courier (the i-th rider). For each rider we must choose exactly one restaurant and one delivery zone.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the restaurant considered for assignment to a rider. Each restaurant must be assigned to exactly one courier.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the delivery patch/zone considered for assignment to a rider. Each delivery zone must be covered by exactly one courier.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Measured riding distance (trip length) for the specific triple (rider, restaurant, delivery zone). The solver should minimize the total sum of these distances across all riders.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of keynote speakers to schedule — which equals the number of available rooms and the number of available time slots. Every speaker must receive exactly one room and one slot.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: A collection of identifiers used for the indices in the instance (e.g., speaker IDs, room IDs, and time-slot IDs). These labels are used to reference speakers, rooms, and slots consistently in the cost entries.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the keynote speaker for this triple — the person being assigned a room and a time slot.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the room assigned to the speaker in this triple. Each room must be used exactly once across all chosen triples.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the time slot assigned to the speaker in this triple. Each time slot must be used exactly once across all chosen triples.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Numeric cost of assigning the given speaker to the given room at the given time slot. The solver selects one triple per speaker so that every room and every time slot is used once and the sum of these costs is minimized.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of products to assign. In this scenario n is also the number of machines and the number of shifts — each index set (products, machines, shifts) has size n.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Labels or identifiers used for the indices appearing in triples. Typically includes the product IDs, machine IDs and shift IDs (for example P1..Pn, M1..Mn, S1..Sn) referenced by the cost entries.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the product in this cost triple (the first index). Each product must be assigned exactly once to a single machine and a single shift.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the machine in this cost triple (the second index). Machines are dedicated: each machine must be used by exactly one product in the final assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the shift in this cost triple (the third index). Shifts are also exclusive: each shift must be assigned to exactly one product.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost of producing the specified product on the specified machine during the specified shift. The goal is to select one triple per product so that each machine and each shift are used once and the sum of these production_cost values is minimized.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of students (which equals the number of projects and the number of supervisors). This is the size of each index set i/j/k.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers (labels) used for the index positions 1..n — the IDs you can use to refer to students, projects and supervisors when enumerating triples.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the student for whom this triple describes an assignment. Exactly one triple must be chosen for each student.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the project assigned to the student in this triple. Each project must be used by exactly one student in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the supervisor assigned to the student in this triple. Each supervisor must mentor exactly one student in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Penalty (cost) for assigning the given student to the given project and supervisor. The assignment solver minimizes the sum of these penalties over all chosen triples.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of models to schedule (equal to the number of photographers and backdrops); the size of each index set.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the models being scheduled (each i corresponds to one model who must be paired with exactly one photographer and one backdrop).

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the model in this triple — the model who would be photographed and later retouched.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the photographer assigned to the model in this triple.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the backdrop assigned to the model in this triple.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Predicted retouch time (cost) if this specific model is shot by this photographer using this backdrop; used to compute total retouch time to minimize.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dining tables (equal to the number of appetizer vendors and dessert vendors). This tells you how many table-to-vendor assignments are required.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Labels used as identifiers for the indices involved (the names/IDs for tables, appetizer vendors, and dessert vendors). Use these IDs when referring to i/j/k values in triples.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the table for this triple. Each table must be assigned exactly one appetizer vendor and one dessert vendor.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the appetizer vendor assigned to the table in this triple. Each appetizer vendor must serve exactly one table overall.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the dessert vendor assigned to the table in this triple. Each dessert vendor must serve exactly one table overall.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Total cost charged if the given table is served by the specified appetizer and dessert vendors (sum of that table's appetizer cost and dessert cost). The solver minimizes the sum of these costs over all tables.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of pallets to be delivered (equal to the number of trucks and the number of routes). This is the problem size: one triple must be chosen for each pallet.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Labels or identifiers used for the indices (e.g., pallet IDs, truck IDs, route IDs). These identifiers reference elements of the i/j/k index sets in the instance data.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the pallet (the first index i). Each pallet must appear in exactly one chosen triple.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the truck assigned to the pallet (the second index j). Each truck can carry at most one pallet and must be used exactly once across all chosen triples.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the delivery route assigned to the pallet (the third index k). Each route must be used by exactly one pallet.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The fuel consumption (cost) if the given pallet is loaded on the given truck and sent along the given route. The solver minimizes the sum of these fuel_cost values over the selected one-to-one matching of pallets, trucks, and routes.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of clients (which is equal to the number of outfits and the number of accessories). There are exactly n clients, n outfits, and n accessories; each client must receive one outfit and one accessory.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of n unique identifiers (labels) used to index the clients, outfits, and accessories (for example 1..n or actual names). These IDs are the values referenced by the client_id, outfit_id, and accessory_id fields.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the client for this triple — the person who would wear the specified outfit and accessory. Exactly one triple must be selected for each client.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the outfit assigned in this triple. Each outfit must be assigned to exactly one client (no outfit sharing).

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the accessory assigned in this triple. Each accessory must be assigned to exactly one client (no accessory sharing).

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The wardrobe cost for giving the specified client (client_id) that outfit (outfit_id) together with that accessory (accessory_id). This is the per-client outfit+accessory price; the solver sums these costs for the selected triples and minimizes the total.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of bands to schedule (which equals the number of available stages and the number of time slots). Each band must receive exactly one stage and one time slot.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers used in the instance: ordered lists of names/IDs for bands, stages, and time slots (each list has length n). For example, band names, stage names, and time-slot labels that the solver can reference.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the band in this cost entry. Each band (i) must be assigned exactly one (stage, time) pair across the chosen triples.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the stage in this cost entry. Each stage must host exactly one band in the final assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the time slot in this cost entry. Each time slot must feature exactly one band in the final assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The expected scheduling-conflict cost if the given band (band_id) is assigned to the given stage (stage_id) at the given time slot (time_slot_id). The solver picks one triple per band to minimize the sum of these costs.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of documents to assign — also the number of translators and the number of language pairs. All three index sets (documents, translators, language pairs) have this same size.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers used to label indices in the instance. Typically this includes the list of document IDs (for i), translator IDs (for j), and language-pair IDs (for k) so each i, j, k refers to a concrete item in the scenario.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the document being assigned in this triple. Each document i must appear in exactly one chosen triple (one seat at the table).

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the translator assigned to the document in this triple. Each translator j may be used for exactly one document across all chosen triples.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the language pair (source→target) used for the document in this triple. Each language pair k must be used for exactly one document.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary fee charged if document i is translated by translator j using language pair k. The solver chooses triples to minimize the sum of these translation fees while respecting the one-to-one constraints.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of customer jobs to process; equal to the number of printers and the number of finishing stations so each printer and each finisher will be assigned exactly one order.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers used for the indices (orders/printers/finishers). Typically a list like [1,...,n] or explicit labels that identify each order, printer and finishing station.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific customer order (the job that must be printed and finished). Each order i must be assigned exactly one printer and one finisher.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific printer that can process an order. In a valid solution every printer j is assigned to exactly one order.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific finishing station (finisher) that will perform the finishing step for an order. In a valid solution every finisher k is assigned to exactly one order.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (time) for assigning order i to printer j and finisher k: the sum of the printing time on printer j for that order plus the finishing time at finisher k. The objective is to choose triples (i,j,k) that minimize the sum of these values over all orders.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of ad campaigns (equal to the number of channels/outlets and the number of weeks). This is the problem size: how many triples must be chosen so each campaign gets one channel and one week and every channel and week is used exactly once.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for the campaigns (the i-index values). Each identifier names a campaign that must be assigned exactly one channel and one week.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The campaign identifier (which campaign is being scheduled). For each campaign_id we must pick exactly one channel_id and one week_id.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The channel/outlet identifier (which outlet would run the campaign). Each channel_id must be assigned to exactly one campaign across the full solution.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The calendar week identifier (which week the campaign would run). Each week_id must be assigned to exactly one campaign across the full solution.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The advertising spend (price) for running the given campaign on the specified channel in the specified week. The solver chooses one triple per campaign to minimize the sum of these combo_cost values under the one-per-channel and one-per-week constraints.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of family members — also the number of distinct chores and the number of cleaning days. Each member, each chore, and each day must be used exactly once.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers (names or labels) for the family members who will be assigned. These labels index the i-dimension: each identifier corresponds to exactly one person to receive a chore and a day.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The family member identifier (one of the member_ids) who would receive this specific assignment triple. Exactly one triple must be chosen for each member.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The household task identifier under consideration for assignment to the given member. Each chore must be assigned to exactly one family member across all chosen triples.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The cleaning day identifier being paired with the member and chore. Every cleaning day must be claimed by exactly one member in the final selection.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The numeric inconvenience (discomfort) score for assigning this particular member to this specific chore on this specific day. The solver seeks the set of triples (one per member) that minimizes the sum of these scores.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of tables to seat (problem size). This equals the number of waiters and the number of wine pairings — i, j, and k index sets all have this size.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers or labels used for the indices in the scenario: names or codes for tables, names or IDs for waiters, and names or codes for wine pairings. These are the labels referenced by the i, j, k fields in the cost data.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific restaurant table (the first index). Each triple chooses exactly one table to receive the listed waiter and wine pairing.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific waiter (the second index). Each waiter must be assigned to exactly one table in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific wine pairing (the third index). Each wine pairing must be matched to exactly one table.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The service-time value (cost) for assigning the given waiter and wine pairing to the given table. The solver minimizes the sum of these service_time values across the chosen triples.

global_fields.scenario_description: The set or list of identifiers used in the instance — labels for the classes, the classrooms, and the teaching assistants. These identifiers index the i/j/k positions (for example: class names, room numbers, TA names) and correspond to the size n.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the class in this triple. In the scenario 'i' denotes the specific class that must be assigned exactly one classroom and one TA.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the classroom in this triple. Each room can be assigned to exactly one class across the full solution.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the teaching assistant in this triple. Each TA can be assigned to exactly one class across the full solution.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Combined running cost of assigning the given class to the given classroom with the given TA (e.g., room overhead + TA time). The objective is to pick n triples (one per class) that use each room and each TA exactly once and minimize the sum of these running_cost values.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of scheduled home visits — which equals the number of nurses available and the number of equipment kits. Use this as the problem size for creating one-to-one assignments.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each scheduled home visit (e.g., V1, V2, ...). These are the primary indices i for which you must choose exactly one nurse and one kit.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of a particular home visit (matches one entry from visit_ids). For each visit i you must select exactly one nurse and one equipment kit.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of a nurse candidate for assignment to the visit. Each nurse must be assigned to exactly one visit across the whole solution.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of an equipment kit candidate to send with the nurse to the visit. Each kit must be used for exactly one visit in the final assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The numeric cost of assigning the specified nurse and equipment kit to the given visit (i,j,k). This reflects travel time, nurse workload, kit suitability, and any other operational expenses; the goal is to choose triples to minimize the sum of these costs.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of exhibit spaces (also the number of artworks and the number of lighting setups). Every space will receive exactly one artwork and one lighting configuration.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The set or list of unique identifiers used to label elements of the index sets (e.g., IDs or names for exhibit spaces, artworks, and lighting options). There should be exactly n identifiers in each index set.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the exhibit space in this candidate assignment triple — which space would receive the given artwork and lighting.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the artwork proposed to be installed in the given space for this triple.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the lighting configuration proposed to be installed in the given space for this triple.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost of installing that particular artwork with that particular lighting setup in that particular exhibit space. The solver will sum these costs across chosen triples to minimize total cost.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of production orders to fulfill — equal to the number of machines and the number of operators available. This is the size of each index set (orders, machines, operators).

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the production orders (one id per order). These labels identify the first index values that must each be matched to exactly one machine and one operator.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the production order in this triple — the order that would be processed by the specified machine and operator.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the machine in this triple — the single machine that would process the given order if this triple is chosen.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the operator in this triple — the single operator who would work on the given order with the specified machine if this triple is chosen.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Numerical processing cost for assigning this specific (order, machine, operator) triple. The solver seeks a one-to-one matching across orders, machines and operators that minimizes the sum of these costs.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of outreach locations to cover; this equals the number of volunteers and the number of vehicles available (the size of the i/j/k index sets).

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The set or list of labels/IDs used to refer to indices in the instance — identifiers for sites, volunteers, and vehicles that will appear as values of i, j, and k in cost entries.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of an outreach location (site). Exactly one triple will be chosen for each site_id.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a volunteer. Each volunteer_id must be assigned to exactly one site (used exactly once across chosen triples).

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a vehicle. Each vehicle_id must be assigned to exactly one site (used exactly once across chosen triples).

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Numeric travel plus coordination cost incurred if the given volunteer (volunteer_id) and vehicle (vehicle_id) are assigned together to the given site (site_id). The objective is to pick one triple per site so the sum of these assignment_cost values is minimized.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of customers (also the number of stylists and fitting rooms). This is the size of each index set so we must make exactly n assignments.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers/labels used for the indices (e.g., customer labels, stylist labels, room labels). These are the index names the triples refer to.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The customer being assigned in this triple. For every customer_id we must choose exactly one triple.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The stylist assigned to the customer in this triple. Each stylist_id may be used in exactly one chosen triple.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The fitting room reserved for the customer in this triple. Each fitting_room_id may be used in exactly one chosen triple.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The combined cost (staffing + space) of assigning this specific customer to this stylist and this fitting room. The solver sums chosen assignment_cost values and minimizes that total.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of screenings to schedule; equals the number of available technicians and the number of projector models (problem size).

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The set or list of identifiers used to label indices (e.g., 1..n or screening codes). These identifiers index screenings, technicians and projector models consistently across the data.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific screening (the first index). For this screening we must choose exactly one technician and one projector model.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific technician (the second index). Each technician may be assigned to exactly one screening in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific projector model (the third index). Each projector model may be used in exactly one screening in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The cost of assigning the given technician and projector model to the given screening (e.g., combined crew and equipment cost). The objective is to pick one triple per screening so the sum of these costs is minimized.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of tasks to staff (this is also the number of developers and the number of test environments). It is the size n of each index set: there are n tasks, n developers and n testing environments.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers (labels) used for the indices in the instance — i.e. the IDs that refer to tasks, developers and test environments (for example 1..n or custom labels). These IDs are used when specifying triples (task, developer, environment).

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific task (the first index). Every triple refers to exactly one task that needs one developer and one test environment.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a developer (the second index). In a chosen triple this developer is assigned to the corresponding task; each developer must be used for exactly one task across the full assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a testing environment (the third index). In a chosen triple this environment is assigned to the corresponding task; each environment must be used for exactly one task across the full assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The cost of assigning the given developer and testing environment to the given task (covers development+testing cost for that triple). The solver sums these costs for all chosen triples and seeks the assignment with minimum total cost.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of incoming students to assign — equal to the number of available dorm rooms and the number of roommate pairing options. This is the problem size (one student, one room, and one roommate option per index).

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Three ordered lists of identifiers, one list for each index set in the order (students, rooms, roommate_options). These give the concrete IDs that appear as values of i, j, k in the cost entries.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the incoming student being assigned in this triple. Exactly one triple must be chosen for each student_id.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the dorm room assigned to the student in this triple. Each room_id may be used in exactly one chosen triple (one student per room).

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the roommate pairing option applied to the student in this triple. Each roommate_option_id may be used in exactly one chosen triple (no pairing option repeated).

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The housing cost (monetary or weighted penalty) of assigning the given student_id to the given room_id with the given roommate_option_id. The solver chooses one triple per student so the sum of these assignment_cost values is minimized.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of landscaping projects (size of each index set). There are this many jobs, suppliers, and delivery dates; every job must receive exactly one supplier and one delivery date.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Labels or identifiers used for the indices (e.g., lists of job IDs, supplier IDs, and delivery-date IDs). These are the concrete names a solver will use to refer to each job, supplier, and delivery slot.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a specific landscaping project that needs assignment to one supplier and one delivery date. Exactly one triple with this job_id must be chosen.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a plant supplier candidate for the given job. Each supplier_id can be assigned to at most one job in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of a delivery slot/date for supplying the job. Each delivery_date_id can be used for at most one job in the final matching.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost of assigning the specified supplier and delivery date to the job (covers plant procurement and delivery on that date). The solver minimizes the sum of these costs over a valid one-to-one matching.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of models to dress (which equals the number of outfits and the number of backstage assistants). This is the size of each index set i/j/k and the number of triples to choose.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers (names or labels) used for the indices: model IDs, outfit IDs, and assistant IDs. These labels identify each model, each outfit, and each backstage assistant in the instance.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the model to be assigned an outfit and an assistant. Each model i must receive exactly one outfit and one assistant.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the outfit that can be assigned to a model. Each outfit j can be worn by exactly one model.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the backstage assistant who can support a model. Each assistant k can support exactly one model.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Total cost incurred if the given model i is assigned outfit j and assistant k. This represents the combined preparation (outfit) and staffing (assistant) cost for that triple.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of reading sessions to schedule; equals the number of storytellers and the number of seating arrangements (so there will be exactly one storyteller and one seating plan per session).

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The labels used to identify items in the index sets (identifiers for sessions, storytellers, and seating layouts). These are the IDs you will see referenced as i (session), j (storyteller), and k (seating plan) in the cost entries.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of a specific reading session for which you must choose one storyteller and one seating layout. In the solution each session_id appears exactly once.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the storyteller assigned to the given session. Each storyteller_id must be used for exactly one session in the final assignment.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the seating arrangement used for the given session. Each seating_layout_id must be used exactly once across all sessions.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (monetary or other resource measure) of assigning the specified storyteller and seating layout to the specified session (i,j,k). The goal is to pick one triple per session so the sum of these assignment_cost values is minimal.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of vendors to place (this is equal to the number of stalls and the number of electricity hookup schedules).

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: The identifiers used in the instance to name indices — e.g., lists or labels for vendors, stalls, and hookup schedules (can be integers or strings) that correspond to i, j, k values.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the vendor to be assigned a stall and a hookup schedule. Exactly one triple is chosen for each vendor.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the market stall assigned to the vendor. Each stall must be assigned to exactly one vendor.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the electricity hookup schedule (time slot / power plan) assigned to the vendor. Each schedule must be assigned to exactly one vendor.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Operating cost incurred if the specified vendor is placed at the specified stall with the specified hookup schedule; the solver minimizes the sum of these costs over chosen triples.

global_fields.name: n
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of clients to schedule — equals the number of photographers and the number of backdrops. The assignment will produce exactly one triple (client, photographer, backdrop) for each of these num_clients.

global_fields.name: ids
global_fields.scenario_description: Readable identifiers for the indices used in the instance. This typically contains three parallel lists or a mapping named 'clients', 'photographers', and 'backdrops', each of length num_clients, giving the labels that correspond to i, j, and k values.

cost_item_fields.name: i
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (from the clients list) of the client being scheduled in this triple. Exactly one triple must be chosen for each client_id.

cost_item_fields.name: j
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (from the photographers list) of the photographer assigned to the client in this triple. Each photographer_id can appear in exactly one chosen triple.

cost_item_fields.name: k
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (from the backdrops list) of the backdrop reserved for the client in this triple. Each backdrop_id can appear in exactly one chosen triple.

cost_item_fields.name: cost
cost_item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost of assigning this specific photographer and backdrop to the specified client (the client's booking plus setup cost). The solver sums these costs over chosen triples and seeks the minimum total.
